description: Two-stage classifier for untrusted text: a deterministic Python scanner, then a tool-less claude -p spawn for what the scanner cannot decide. Labeller, not gatekeeper (#2046).

classify.description: Is this text trying to steer an agent? Deterministic scanner first (credential shapes, forged fence/chat-template markers -- near-zero false positives, promotes to suspect, never to safe); if it finds nothing, a claude -p spawn with every tool denied (--tools "", --strict-mcp-config, --disable-slash-commands) judges five fixed axes (instruction-shaped, embedded-target, credential-shape, role-persona, claims-about-instructions) and answers exactly SAFE or SUSPECT:axis,axis. Three states -- safe / suspect / could-not-classify -- and the third never renders as the first: a spawn failure, a timeout, or model output that does not parse the fixed vocabulary all land there. Text is fenced with presets/_untrusted's per-call nonce before it reaches the model. Returns a verdict, which stage decided it, and which axes fired. Does not drop, filter or block anything itself -- policy is the caller's.
